flawed_step: Step 4: Inferring P(X>Z)>1/2 from P(X>Y)>1/2 and P(Y>Z)>1/2. The preceding valid argument only gives P(X>Z)>0 because {X>Y}∩{Y>Z}⊆{X>Z}.
counterexample: Let X=0 surely. Independently, let Y=-1 with probability 0.6 and Y=100 with probability 0.4; let Z=-2 with probability 0.25 and Z=50 with probability 0.75. Then P(X>Y)=0.6 and P(Y>Z)=0.55, but P(X>Z)=0.25.
assessment_summary: The relation is not transitive. The two majority-probability comparisons can overlap on only a small set, and mutual independence of X,Y,Z does not make the events {X>Y} and {Y>Z} independent because both involve Y.
